summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including sclerosing mesenteritis, chronic abdominal pain, and migraines was admitted for acute on chronic anemia discovered during a routine exam. She had recently undergone g-tube removal and reported increasing fatigue and migraine frequency. Initial evaluation revealed a hemoglobin of 7.6 g/dL, prompting a blood transfusion. Imaging showed no acute bleed, but an endoscopy identified a bleeding arteriovenous malformation in the mid-jejunum, which was successfully cauterized. She received IV iron and had her PPI dose increased. Her hemoglobin improved to 9.2 g/dL by discharge. Migraine-related stuttering and twitching occurred but resolved spontaneously. Hypoglycemia was managed with dextrose-containing fluids. She was discharged home with stable vital signs, instructions to monitor for GI bleed symptoms, and follow-up labs to track her hemoglobin.
